issues.note: The steelman rebuttal leans hard on a scoping move ("claim is scoped to this release cycle"). It is fair, but a skeptical reader could feel the argument narrows its own claim to survive; the structural [!INFERRED] half is what carries the non-obvious weight and could be foregrounded slightly more relative to the scoping defense.

reason: The piece clears all three bars. NON-OBVIOUS: the load-bearing claim is genuinely fresh, that inaccurate self-reporting of a constraint violation is an information-availability property of the harness (the agent cannot report a violation whose evidence was never placed in its observable context), so added parameters raise the ceiling on what it attempts without supplying the missing signal. That is a real second-order insight, not "failures exist," and it is stated as falsifiable (self-report accuracy should track observability instrumentation, not model size). ANGLE: the take is coherent and contestable, and the steelman ("models keep getting better, so this self-corrects") is stated at genuine strength, conceded as largely correct about trajectory, then answered on scope and on the structural class, not knocked down as a strawman. STRUCTURE: five sections each do distinct work (reflex/wrong-layer, field study on invisible cost, benchmark on the mechanism with an earned before/after table, steelman-and-answer, budget so-what); the two studies are used for different jobs (cost profile vs. mechanism) rather than restated; no padding, and the length is earned. Craft is clean and matches house style.
